The fee schedules of the four agencies ordering from this seller pay $175 per completed loan signing (fee schedules, Nov 2026).

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE stance is supported for a net-contribution target. The 32 signings are under signed standing orders from four title agencies (buyerVolume EVIDENCE, 32 written acceptances at $175) and the $175 comes from the agencies' own fee schedules — a real purchase price for these buyers. The recorded fulfiller is Tri-County Signing Agents Network at a written $95 per signing, payable only within 3 days after the agency pays, so no capital goes out before cash comes in (exposure $0 fits the $0 cap). Recomputed: net $80 per signing; 32 x $80 = $2,560 >= $2,000; 25 signings suffice (25 x 80 = $2,000), so 7 cancellations can be absorbed. Timing: signings days 2-16 at up to 6/day (32 over 15 days averages ~2.1/day); 10 days to cash puts the last agency receipt at day 26 and the last Tri-County payment at day 29, both inside 30, so the whole contribution settles in the window. Ledger: $5,600 received, $3,040 paid, $2,560 net, minimum cash $1,280 on day 22 — never negative.
findings: Arithmetic verified: 2 x 16 x $175 = $5,600 receipts; 2 x 16 x $95 = $3,040 supplier payments; net $2,560 against the $2,000 contribution target.

Settlement: day-16 signings pay by day 26 and Tri-County is paid by day 29; the contribution is fully net within the 30-day window with one day of margin — a late agency payment on the last batch would push the supplier payment, not the receipt, past day 30, but the receipts alone already settle in time.

Capacity: the card states the 32 signings are scheduled across days 2-16 but not their per-day distribution; if any day carries more than 6, Tri-County's cap would delay a signing. The 7-signing slack covers a few such slips.
Owner hours: the card records 0.2 human hours per signing (~6.4 h for coordination) while ownerHours is null; the contract sets no hours ceiling, so this does not bind.
